name: Interpolant Induced by Marching Cases
definition: A method to construct piecewise-polynomial splines (or their non-polynomial equivalents) that correspond exactly to the contours generated by standard Marching Squares/Cubes cases, allowing for the computation of geometric properties (area, volume) as continuous functions of the isovalue, rather than discrete approximations.
summary: Interpolant Induced by Marching Cases constructs continuous splines matching standard Marching Squares or Cubes contours, enabling geometric analysis across isovalue ranges via a finite state machine approach.
